Subject: Clarify API billing: Chat vs Responses vs legacy endpoints

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday — really appreciate NeoRetail's thoughtful questions. I'm attaching our Q1 rate card and a tiny usage sample so we can align on a baseline. Before we jump to numbers, a couple of quick clarifications so we price the right thing:

- Can you confirm which Redwood endpoints your engineering team is calling today? Specifically: /v1/chat/completions (chat API), /v1/responses (new Responses API), or legacy /v1/completions (older completions endpoint).
- Do you use system messages and assistant message roles heavily (multi-role chat), or are you primarily sending prompt-only requests and getting a single text output?
- Any rough monthly token volumes or peak qps you expect (ballpark is fine).

To avoid surprises: our billing counts both input + output tokens for the Responses SKU. The Chat-completions SKU also counts tokens but has different per-token rates tied to the conversation primitives and streaming behavior. The legacy completions endpoint uses legacy pricing tiers (we can map those to Responses if you prefer a single bill).

If helpful I can put together a short table with concrete example calls and the estimated token math. Want me to do that and drop it here, or would you prefer a quick 20-min call with Jonas to walk through?

Attachments: Redwood_RateCard_Q1_2026.pdf (rate card summary), usage_example_sample.csv (sample tokenization of a few calls)

Best,

Samir — looping in a couple extra details to make the math concrete. Below are simplified rules we apply and a tiny example table (attached as endpoint_billing_table.txt).

Billing rules (short):
- Responses API (/v1/responses): billed as "responses" SKU. Cost is per input_token + output_token. Streaming doesn't change token accounting — charges are for tokens actually emitted and received. If connection drops mid-stream, tokens already generated are billed.
- Chat Completions (/v1/chat/completions): billed as "chat" SKU. We aggregate across messages; system and user messages are tokenized and billed as input tokens; assistant outputs billed as output tokens. In practice unit rates for chat differ slightly from Responses because chat pricing accounts for conversation state and additional metadata.
- Legacy Completions (/v1/completions): legacy SKU. For new customers we recommend mapping calls to Responses; for migration we provide a transitional rate mapping so you can forecast.

Example (approx):
- Single-turn prompt: user=100 tokens, model replies=400 tokens -> Responses bill = 500 tokens; Chat bill = input 100 + output 400 = 500 tokens (same token count; per-token price differs by SKU).
- Multi-message chat: system=50, user1=80, user2=60, assistant reply=300 -> total billed tokens = 490 (sum of all tokens).

Discount ladder (indicative, negotiable):
- Commit >= $50k/mo: 5% discount
- Commit >= $150k/mo: 10% discount + dedicated SLA
- Commit >= $400k/mo: 18% discount + priority capacity

I attached the little table mapping a few call types to the billing SKU. If you can share a sample of your traffic (the usage_example_sample.csv Marissa attached is perfect), we can model the monthly spend and show where you fall in the ladder.

LMK if you want me on the call Wednesday morning.

—Jonas

Samir — thanks for the questions and for the availability window. Short answers and next steps: 

1) Yes — both system and user messages are tokenized and billed as input; assistant outputs are billed as output. Streaming: you pay for tokens actually produced (if stream cut early, tokens produced until that point are billed).
2) Chat has the same token counting logic but different per-token pricing and sometimes small per-request meta fees for very high qps enterprise plans; we'll surface that if it becomes relevant for your predicted qps.
3) Migration from /v1/completions -> /v1/responses: token math is equivalent, but Rates differ by SKU. We'll produce a migration spend model so you can see the delta.

Next steps:
- Jonas will model your 30M tokens/mo sample against the rate card and share an estimated monthly invoice and discount tier.
- I'll schedule a 20-min call Wed 3/11 at 9:00am PST (confirmed) to walk through the model and procurement questions.
- I'll drop a HubSpot link and a draft MSA/DocuSign if you want to get procurement started while we finalize terms.

See you tomorrow — call invite sent.
